title.narrative: PROTECTING JAGUAR HABITAT THROUGH ECOTOURISM IN THE LACANDONA REGION IN CHIAPAS, MEXICO.

description.narrative: The project "Protecting Endangered Habitat through Nature Tourism in the Lacandon Region in Chiapas, Mexico" supports the conservation of the tropical rainforest of the Lacandon jungle of Mexico by addressing the impacts of uncontrolled and unsustainable agricultural expansion in the forests of the indigenous communities of Naha, Metzabok and Las Nubes. The Lacandon jungle represents the largest rainforest in North America and is home of endangered species such as jaguars, tapirs, peccaries, and harpy eagles. This two-year assistance award will enable Eco-Creando Soluciones, A.C. to create non-extractive economies based on nature-tourism that will generate alternative economic opportunities that rely on the local communities' ability to conserve their primary forests and preserve wildlife. Specific activities include: (1) building the communities capacities to establish and manage seven nature tourism enterprises so they meet visitor ready standards; (2) co-creating experiential tourism products linked to the natural ecosystems and local culture; (3) connecting community enterprises with nature tourism markets to make nature tourism a viable alternative livelihood; (4) enhancing facilities and providing equipment to improve nature tourism services; (5) facilitating participatory workshops to reach voluntary conservation agreements with communities and promote the reforestation of degraded lands; and (6) monitoring forest cover, connectivity, and ecological integrity to assess effectiveness of the project activities.
